Subject: [ALERT] Latency + error rate spike: production inference (elm-frontend)

Hi Lauren / Redwood,

We're seeing a sharp increase in p99 latency (from ~220ms to 2.8s) and a concurrent spike in 502/504 errors for the elm-frontend inference route after the maintenance window this morning. Error volume began ~06:50 PDT and has persisted across the US region. Throughput is down ~30% and customer-facing failures are visible in our dashboard.

We rolled no changes on our side. Can you confirm whether a model rollout, quant profile change, or config flip occurred on Redwood around 06:45-07:00 PDT? This is impacting triage and physician-facing flows.

Attaching traces and sample requests. Please escalate—we'll need an ETA to resolution.

Sanjay Patel

Elmwood Health

Subject: Re: [ALERT] Latency + error rate spike: production inference (elm-frontend)

Sanjay—thanks for the quick heads up and the attached traces. We're looking into it now.

Prelim: we had an automated regional rollout of model v2.3 with a new mixed quant profile (q4a per-host, q2a on edge pools) during the 06:30–07:00 maintenance window. That rollout should have been gated for Elmwood (pinned to v2.2) but it looks like a routing policy mismatch allowed v2.3 to reach one AZ serving Elmwood traffic.

I've looped in Rishi (runtime) and Marissa (customer success / escalation) to triage. We'll update within 30 minutes with a mitigation plan. If you'd like, we can stand up a bridge—what's the best contact number?

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 08:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: [ALERT] Latency + error rate spike: production inference (elm-frontend)

Quick triage notes (runtime):
- Confirmed: v2.3 mixed-quant profile deployed in us-west-2 during the window. Traffic split incorrectly applied to a subset of Elmwood's edge pool (approx 18% of requests).
- Symptom: q2a micro-dequant path is introducing extra decode stalls under long prompt shapes used by Elmwood (clinical summaries). KV-cache path also saw cache miss amplification due to a minor change in tokenization between v2.2 and v2.3.
- Effects: P99 spikes, ~30% throughput drop, increased 5xx from model timeouts and higher decoding memory pressure.

Mitigation options:
1) Immediate: roll traffic back to v2.2 for Elmwood in affected AZs (fastest, low risk).
2) Short term: apply per-pool quant profile override to force q4a for Elmwood's edge pool (may recover latency but risks slight accuracy delta).
3) Longer: revert the tokenization delta + re-run kv-cache warmers for Elmwood prompts before re-rollout.

I recommend option 1 now, followed by option 3 for stability. We have a rollback runbook ready (attached). Need an approval to execute global rollback for Elmwood in us-west-2. ETA to full rollback: ~12 minutes once started.

Rishi
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
